intervention.statement: Actual baseline supports a focused tile-granularity experiment. Mean per-launch core ratios (five calls per case) for vector/scalar/MTE2 are case1 0.703/0.302/0.161, case8 0.495/0.342/0.349, case14 0.539/0.314/0.345, case20 0.738/0.266/0.177. Scalar and input-transfer work is material, particularly in tanh. Source issues queue and vector API setup per 1024 elements. Enlarging to4096 lowers repeated tile work with known UB headroom without changing math or core partition. The hypothesis is plausible, not yet a causal bottleneck finding.

knowledge.classification_note: Only explicit recorded accesses are knowledge reads; machine evidence and retrospective curator facts are separate.

next_decision.reason: Two measured interventions have reduced tile overhead. gelu002 adds mode-targeted gains with20/20 standalone/prepared correctness and successful runtime. Remaining exact case20 vector ratio0.851725 limits the evidence for further overhead work; tanh case8/14 vector ratios0.619331/0.747766 still leave possible opportunity, but pipe ratios do not establish overlap loss or actionable API redundancy. Larger FP32 tanh tile16384 would require327680 explicit bytes, above196608UB; simply duplicating8192 input/output buffers needs229376bytes. A next intervention therefore requires a new lifetime/schedule or numerical/API argument not established by current evidence. Freeze both actual candidates for full-case evaluation rather than extend the source search without a sufficiently supported mechanism. This is not a claim of optimality.
